assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near quantum-mechanical accuracy at force-field cost, so reactions, phase behaviour and condensed-phase free energies can be simulated at scales that were out of reach. This is a genuine game-changer for atomistic simulation and already has real consequences across catalysis, materials and increasingly biomolecular modelling. As a simulation specialist I weigh the quantitative link to experiment heavily, and the validation record is now substantial.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello (2007, neural-network potentials) opened the field; Csányi with Bartók (Gaussian approximation potentials, SOAP descriptors) made the second independent foundational line. Bartók, von Lilienfeld and E are important but the three-person limit makes Behler, Parrinello and Csányi the cleanest core, with Bartók's share in GAP an unavoidable hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: many independent groups, widespread production use, and foundation-type models are appearing. Computation was recognised in 2013 and 2024, so some committee fatigue is possible, but this is a different, enabling methodology.
uncertainties: Whether Bartók's role in GAP deserves a seat over Csányi or Parrinello is a hard credit call.
Transferability and extrapolation reliability of universal models are still being established.
Committee may feel computational chemistry was recently rewarded (2024).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation of proteins is a completely new pharmacological modality: instead of inhibiting a target, one recruits an E3 ligase to remove it. It is conceptually simple, chemically elegant and has produced clinical candidates, a clear case of a new idea with demonstrated consequences.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the first PROTAC (2001) and Crews drove the field through the following decades; Ciulli delivered the VHL ligands and structural rational design that made PROTACs drug-like. Handa, Ito and others established the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, a parallel strand that cannot all be honoured in three seats.
assessment.maturity: Strong and growing clinical validation, though no PROTAC is yet an approved drug as far as I know, so there is a mild question of whether the prize is slightly early.
uncertainties: Approval status of the first PROTAC drugs is uncertain to me.
Molecular glues (cereblon) versus bifunctional PROTACs may require different recognition.
Relation to the 2004 ubiquitin prize needs careful framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view explains how proteins fold quickly and reliably despite a vast conformational space, and links theory to experiment through phi-value analysis and kinetics. It is foundational to how chemists think about biomolecular folding, and ties directly to prediction methods recognised in 2024.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes (1987) set out the framework, Onuchic and Wolynes developed the funnel picture, and Fersht provided the decisive experimental kinetic and mutational approach. Dill and others contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model views, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are firmly accepted and textbook material for decades. The prize would be late rather than early, which is acceptable, though a theory-heavy recognition requires a clear tie to concrete consequences.
uncertainties: Several-way priority dispute among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Bryngelson.
Whether it is a discrete discovery or a conceptual framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically encoding noncanonical amino acids with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets chemists put arbitrary chemistry into proteins in living cells. It is a simple-in-principle but powerful and widely used technology with real downstream consequences in biophysics, enzymology and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues, with Lei Wang as first author of the 2001 breakthrough, started the approach; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms, quadruplet codons and whole-genome recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl are also credited and add to the allocation difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation and broad adoption. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether Wang or Yokoyama or Mehl should be preferred over Chin or Schultz.
Overlap with the 2018 evolution and 2024 protein-design prizes in biochemical engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers transformed photovoltaics research, taking efficiencies from a few percent to above 25% in little over a decade, with a new class of defect-tolerant materials. It is clearly a game-changer in scale of effort and results.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka (2009) made the first perovskite-sensitised cells, Park (2012) and Snaith (2012) showed solid-state high-efficiency devices; Grätzel and Seok were major contributors and prime alternates. Credit among many strong figures is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency data are well reproduced, but long-term stability and lead toxicity remain open, so real-world consequences are still not demonstrated; this may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercial viability not yet proven.
Allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing changed biology and medicine by reducing the cost of a genome by orders of magnitude. The sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry with reversible terminators is an inherently chemical invention with extraordinary consequences.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa chemistry; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing platform was the first commercial massively parallel system, while Mayer and Ju are further credited. The three-person limit forces a difficult choice.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature; long after the impact became obvious. Sequencing was recognised in 1980 and in related ways, so a framing issue exists.
uncertainties: Whether this is better placed as Medicine/Physiology than Chemistry.
Priority disputes between 454, Solexa and Lynx/Mayer technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural and mechanistic understanding of nitrogenase, the enzyme that reduces N2 to ammonia, addresses a central problem of biological chemistry. The FeMo-cofactor structure with its interstitial carbide is a striking fundamental result, relevant to catalysis and enzymology that I care about.
assessment.attribution: Rees and colleagues solved the MoFe protein structure and Einsle's high-resolution work revealed the central carbon; Dean contributed the genetics and biochemical foundation. Seefeldt and Ribbe are strong alternates, and many contributors make a fair three-person set difficult.
assessment.maturity: Structure is solid but the catalytic mechanism is still not settled, so the story is incomplete and recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The mechanism of N2 reduction remains debated.
Credit is spread among many groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled practical delivery of siRNA and mRNA, and billions of vaccine doses show the real-world consequence. The physical chemistry of lipid self-assembly and pKa-tuned ionizable lipids is a real chemical advance.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope built the lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid principles; Anderson and Langer made later lipid discovery contributions; MacLachlan and Madden also appear. Credit is shared across academic and company teams.
assessment.maturity: Impact is demonstrated by approved products, but the 2023 Medicine prize already recognised mRNA vaccines, which may reduce appetite.
uncertainties: Company versus academic credit and patent disputes.
